newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs hit by fears of bond sales.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs hit by fears of bond sales.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen futures fell in line with a slide in Japanese government bond (JGB) futures on Friday following comments by a senior Japanese life insurance industry official.
Kenjiro Hata, chairman of the Life Insurance Association of Japan, was quoted as saying some life insurers might sell domestic and foreign bonds and stocks if Tokyo stock prices did not recover.
"The JGBs lost about 20-30 points on the back of that comment," said a trader with a European futures house.
The March JGB contract settled at 125.70 against its previous 126.15. September Euroyen was quoted at 99.29 at 1105 GMT against its IMM close at 99.31. It saw a low of 99.28.
"JGBs have rallied quite strongly since the year started so it's quite normal there should be some profit-taking," said a European bank dealer.
He said the recent flight to the bond market due to steep losses in Tokyo stocks had also eased as the Nikkei share index appeared to have found a base for the time being.
The Nikkei average ended 54.30 points lower but above the 18,000 support level at 18,090.04.

"Japanese monetary policy should stay steady for the rest of the year so any falls in Euroyen will just give players a chance to get back in," he said, adding that September was likely to trade a 99.26-99.34 range over the next week.

Eurodollar futures finished little changed after overnight declines on the back of comments by Federal Reserve governor Laurence Meyer, who said risks to the U.S. economy were "a little" bit toward the upside, fuelling fears of a rate hike.
"My bias is that the Fed will tighten at some point but not too much and not too many (times)," said the trader with the European bank.
He added that he would still buy Eurodollars on dips as they had overpriced a rate hike.
September Eurodollars finished at 93.98 against their IMM close at 93.97 after trading a four-tick band on above-average turnover of 17,045 lots.
